resolved_during_review.title: Released focus leaves glyph and target labels inconsistent
resolved_during_review.why_it_matters: After holding REC on strip 1, holding REC on strip 2, then releasing strip 2, the top-bar effect glyph switches back to strip 1 while the key number and footer still identify strip 2 and its effect. The next arrow edits strip 1, so the player sees conflicting destinations immediately before changing a mapping. Resolve one displayed held target for the glyph, key number and FX footer together, or move the popup focus to the remaining held button on release.
evidence: Scenario: NoteOn 0 shows strip 1 / REVERB; NoteOn 1 replaces smc_ui.action=1 and strip=1 with strip 2 / DELAY. NoteOff 1 clears its hold but does not update smc_ui.action or strip. Header fallback returns note 0, yet footer and key number still read note/strip 1. smc_fx_held_note() then returns only note 0, so the arrow modifies strip 1.
smc_release() at lines 2025-2031 only extends the popup expiry if no keys remain and releases FX ownership; it never refreshes the displayed action target after a key-up.
resolved_during_review.resolution: Caller applied source/test correction during review; no remaining supported source concern.

validation.reason: Original evidence proves a new display-target inconsistency: after NoteOn 0, NoteOn 1, NoteOff 1, the added header resolver selects held note 0, while the original release path leaves smc_ui.action and strip at note 1; the footer and strip number therefore disagree with the next arrow's actual target. The current caller-applied fix closes this issue statically: after release and any navigation cleanup, it transfers only the active same-peer action popup whose focused key was released to a remaining physically held, FX-owned note through smc_fx_show, updating both action and strip. The footer then reads that note's owned bus, effect and pinned page, matching the glyph and edit selector. The added held_fx_header sequence asserts focus returns to note 0 and the next arrow edits its cell. No material remaining source concern for this finding; tests were inspected only, not executed.

resolved_during_review.title: USB User-mode FX holds cannot claim arrow edits
resolved_during_review.why_it_matters: A performer using the supported USB/peripheral-BLE User-preset input without a central BLE link can play and hold an FX button, but the new chord never remaps it: SMC arrows fall through to page changes and keyboard arrows generate SELECT steps. smc.up describes only the central link, while the existing host queue dispatches physical note presses independently of that flag. Use the physical held bitmap and owned key_bus to admit the target, or explicitly admit peer-zero User-host ownership, while retaining the existing disconnect cleanup and context guards.
evidence: firmware/src/app/smc_mixer.c:2274-2275 -- if (proj.set.bt & PROJ_BT_SMC_USER) smc_message(msg, sizeof msg, allow);
firmware/src/app/smc_mixer.c:330-332 -- USB or peripheral BLE User-preset input uses a separate host MIDI ring; smc_midi_host accepts it without requiring the central link.

Trace: User-mode physical NoteOn reaches smc_button -> smc_fx_try and sets held/key_bus/fx_down; host Right reaches smc_fx_arrow -> smc_fx_held_note -> !smc.up rejection, then normal smc_page_set. smc_fx_keyboard_arrow uses the same rejected selector, so arw_frame returns the ordinary SELECT detent.

validation.reason: Original evidence proves a new routing bug: smc.up is assigned from the central BLE link, whereas enabled User-mode channel-16 host messages reach smc_message and establish physical/FX ownership without that link. The original !smc.up condition in the new shared held-note selector rejects that valid hold for both controller and keyboard arrows. The current caller-applied fix closes this issue statically by removing only the central-link condition while retaining readiness, context, modal/busy/performance, physical-held and owned-bus checks; existing link/preset/release-loss cleanup still clears stale ownership. The added held_fx_host_arrows explicitly disconnects central BLE, asserts !smc.up, sends channel-16 host NoteOn and Right through smc_midi_host, checks the mapping step, checks a keyboard Left step, and releases through the host path. No material remaining source concern for this finding; tests were inspected only, not executed.
